title: The reusable spaceship that made space MORE expensive

dataset.name: Cost to launch 1 kg to low Earth orbit
dataset.units: USD per kg, 2021 dollars, by first launch year

chart.yLabel: Cost per kg to orbit (2021 $, log scale)

segments.text: NASA's reusable Space~Shuttle cost ^more per kilo than the {Saturn V|Saturn Five} it replaced.
A {1965|nineteen sixty-five} Delta~E rocket? About {$178,000|a hundred seventy-eight thousand dollars} per kilo.
The giant {Saturn V|Saturn Five}? About {$5,400|fifty-four hundred}. Bigger rockets tended to be ^cheaper.

beats.chip: Bigger rockets tend to cost less per kg

segments.text: Then the ^reusable Shuttle: about {$65,000|sixty-five thousand}, counting the whole program. Even per flight, no bargain.
The real drop came from rockets designed around ^cost. Today's {Falcon 9|Falcon Nine}: {$2,600|twenty-six hundred}. Falcon~Heavy, at list price: {$1,500|fifteen hundred}.
That's {99%|ninety-nine percent} cheaper than a {1960s|nineteen-sixties} Delta, and a big reason today's satellite boom is possible.

beats.bigSub: per kg vs. the 1965 Delta E

segments.text: Reusable was never the magic word. ^Cheap ^reuse ^was.

beats.cardLine: Reusable was never the magic word.
